blocks.text:
After breakfast, you will set out on a sightseeing tour of the capital. Begin in La Candelaria, the historic district with colonial houses, churches and narrow streets.

Next, visit the Gold Museum, home to a large collection of pre-Hispanic goldwork and more than 20,000 artefacts from the pre-Columbian period. Continue to the Casa de la Moneda, the 17th-century mint, and the Fernando Botero Museum. Its collection includes works by Botero and European artists, including Dalí.

The walk continues to Plaza de Bolívar, with its cathedral and government buildings. If your route passes the presidential palace at around 5 p.m., you may see the changing of the guard.

Finally, take the funicular up Monserrate, rising approximately 500 metres above the city. Here you will find a 17th-century shrine to the Black Madonna and viewpoints overlooking Bogotá.

The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays; the Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum are closed on Tuesdays. Return to the hotel after lunch.
